newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Socialists confirm ban on arms to Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: France's Socialists confirm ban on arms to Taiwan.

text.p: French Defence Minister Alain Richard said on Thursday that the new Socialist government would adhere to a three-year-old agreement with China to end arms sales to Taiwan.
"France has made an agreement with the People's Republic of China. There will be no fresh sales," Richard told RTL radio in an interview.
His comments were believed to be the first on the issue since Socialist Lionel Jospin took over as prime minister last June following the conservatives' election defeat.
Paris agreed in 1994 to stop arming Taiwan after Beijing, which regards the island as a rebel province, closed down the French consulate in Guangzhou and froze French firms out of Chinese contracts.
Before the ban, Taiwan had ordered six missile frigates and 60 Mirage 2000-5 Mirage fighters with air-to-air MICA missiles.

At least the first two of the radar-evading navy frigates and some of the fighters and missiles were delivered before President Jacques Chirac paid a state visit to China last May which produced business deals worth some $1.8 billion for French firms.
